Researcher notes: T1: Both sources are official or authoritative (Ofgem, Citizens Advice) and neither shows a date. Gaps: pass-through/flexible contracts are covered only by Ofgem's brief description, with no detail on non-commodity cost pass-through. There is no Energy Ombudsman page on brokers, no GOV.UK page, and no regulatory detail on commission disclosure rules for non-microbusinesses. Advantages, risks and use cases are partly inferred from the definitions. The search limit was reached, so these gaps remain.
T2: Cost components and levy/VAT facts are covered from Ofgem, HMRC and GOV.UK. Not covered because the search and page limits were reached: (1) an authoritative explanation of which charges (DUoS/TNUoS, BSUoS, RO/FiT/CfD/capacity market levies) are fixed versus pass-through in business contracts, (2) a detailed official Ofgem or DNO breakdown of network charges, and (3) any numeric standard or reduced VAT rate, which doesn't appear in the extracted text of the VAT notice. The VAT notice shows October 2026 dates and describes a temporary zero rate, so check currency before relying on it. The CCL page was last updated 27 November 2025.
T3: Not covered: the primary licence conditions or legislation text (for example the exact rollover rules and the termination fee rules for non-microbusinesses), and the Energy Ombudsman's broker/TPI page, which has the broker award limit and the TPI complaint route. Developments after April 2024 on Ofgem's TPI rules were not checked in detail beyond Ofgem's blog of 31 March 2026. The page limit was reached.
T4: Not answered: practical official guidance on meter type, half-hourly versus non-half-hourly metering and how to find an MPAN or consumption data. The Ofgem half-hourly guidance page (S9) opened with collapsed content and no usable text. Also missing: how supplier credit checks and deposits work in practice, and supplier financial stability checks. Search and page-open limits were reached.
T5: Covered: ESOS (GOV.UK), REGO (Ofgem), the non-domestic smart meter framework (DESNZ consultation), Ofgem's commentary on volatility, and VAT/CCL reliefs. Not covered because limits were reached: Energy Intensive Industries support schemes, SECR thresholds and rules, a detailed authoritative purchasing strategy (such as block and index or flexible buying), and how a business should verify a green tariff beyond the REGO and Fuel Mix Disclosure basics. The smart meter source is a consultation, not final rules.

metadata.rationale: Coverage is good overall. All five tasks have findings from mostly official sources (Ofgem, GOV.UK/HMRC, Energy Ombudsman, Citizens Advice, and the UIA trade body).
